record.paper_title: Boundary and Defect CFT: Open Problems and Applications
record.original_question: Can the relevant boundary conditions for the free fermion and for the super-Virasoro minimal model SVIR3 be derived directly from first principles, or alternatively by adapting the methods of Novak and Runkel?

evidence.quote: It would be interesting to derive the boundary conditions for the free fermion and SVIR3 from first principles or using the methods of Novak and Runkel [84].

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider two two-dimensional conformal field theories: (i) the free fermion theory of central charge c = 1/2, and (ii) the super-Virasoro minimal model commonly denoted SVIR3, i.e. the third unitary N=1 superconformal minimal model with central charge c = 7/10 (the superconformal description of the tri-critical Ising model). Each of these is a local fermionic CFT, and each admits a finite collection of conformal boundary conditions that preserve the relevant chiral symmetry (Virasoro/super-Virasoro plus fermion parity), as well as conformal defects which, via the folding trick, correspond to boundary conditions in the tensor square of the theory.

Problem. Derive, from first principles of (boundary) conformal field theory — for example by solving the sewing/Cardy-Lewellen consistency constraints, classifying module categories over the relevant chiral vertex superalgebra, or applying a defect-construction procedure analogous to the one realizing conformal defects in a fermionic CFT as boundary conditions in the folded theory (i.e. an extension to the super/fermionic setting of the method that constructs new conformal, non-topological and non-factorised defects of a rational CFT as boundary states of its tensor-square) — the complete set of conformal boundary conditions (boundary states) for:

(a) the free fermion CFT (c = 1/2), and
(b) the super-Virasoro minimal model SVIR3 (c = 7/10),

including in each case the explicit boundary state expansions in terms of Ishibashi states and the verification that the resulting open-string spectra (annulus partition functions / NIM-rep coefficients) are non-negative integers compatible with modular covariance and with fermion-number selection rules.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem of deriving the full set of conformal boundary conditions for the free fermion and for the super-Virasoro minimal model SVIR3 from first principles (or by adapting Novak–Runkel's folding-trick construction of defects-as-boundaries in fermionic CFTs) does not appear to have been carried out in the literature. Novak–Runkel's framework treats defects in the tri-critical Ising / SVIR3 model and the related "Fermionic CFTs and classifying algebras" program gives partial classifications, but a first-principles derivation of these specific boundary conditions has not been reported. The problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Defects in the Tri-critical Ising model
status_evidence.snippet: Novak and Runkel construct conformal defects in the fermionic SVIR3 model by realizing them as boundary states in the folded theory.
status_evidence.claim: Provides the Novak–Runkel methodology referenced in the problem, but does not give a first-principles classification of all boundary conditions for the free fermion and SVIR3.

status_evidence.title: Fermionic CFTs and classifying algebras
status_evidence.snippet: Develops the framework of classifying algebras for boundary conditions in fermionic CFTs.
status_evidence.claim: Provides partial general theory but does not derive explicitly the requested SVIR3 and free-fermion boundary states from first principles.

status_evidence.title: Spin from defects in two-dimensional quantum field theory
status_evidence.snippet: Novak–Runkel general construction of spin/fermionic CFT data from defects.
status_evidence.claim: Provides the methods whose adaptation is suggested but does not itself supply the SVIR3 derivation.
